rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body; this is a concrete-teacher lecture (figure + definitional bullets + pointer to two reads), not a live-demo beat.

Every chunk carries a self-carrying claim: chunk 1 defines skill/footprint against the figure; chunk 2 names four wiring mechanisms plus the checks/routes point; chunk 3 states composition is unsettled and points to two reads. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 1 header 'A skill's footprint is where its job lands' (line 5) matches bullet 2's claim verbatim in substance (line 10: 'Its footprint is wherever the job lands'). Chunk 2 header 'From skills to a workflow' (line 13) truthfully names the composition-mechanics content that follows. Chunk 3 header 'Composition is a live argument, so you read' (line 22) matches its own first sentence almost verbatim (line 24).

Checked each sub-item across all chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found; the chunk-2 four-item list (line 17: 'an explicit load'/'an orchestrator'/'routing'/'a hand-off') is a definitional enumeration where each item carries distinct new content, not an anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative anywhere (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing); no number-with-retraction pattern; no abstraction-noun stack (concrete nouns throughout: skill, footprint, pier, leg, seam); no empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/authorial dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) found in body. 'skill', 'footprint', 'orchestrator', 'leaf', 'routing', 'hand-off', 'pilot' are all defined in-body as house-taught workflow vocabulary for AE101's engineer-IC register, not maintainer-internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 2 (line 17) carries 5 bold handles on one slide (an explicit load / an orchestrator / routing / a hand-off / leaf), over the stated '≤1 bolded element on most slides' default. This qualifies under the rule's own exception: 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' — the slide's entire job is to name and consolidate the four wiring mechanisms (plus leaf), one handle per mechanism, matching the maintainer block's explicit design note (line 34 of raw source: 'slide 2: the four wiring mechanisms... plus leaf at its definition'). Chunk 1 carries 2 handles (skill, footprint) across two separate bullets with the third bullet plain — also within the consolidation reading, as both are the slide's two core coined terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lecture, so all ## headings should be claims, not imperative/phase labels. Closest call: chunk 2 header 'From skills to a workflow' (line 13) is a topic-transition phrase rather than a strict subject+verb claim like chunk 1's 'A skill's footprint is where its job lands' or chunk 3's 'Composition is a live argument, so you read'. It is not imperative and not a numbered phase label (the two shapes the rule actually bans for a lecture), and the maintainer block (raw source line 51) explicitly names and accepts it as the header that 'names the composition concept the slide teaches in its variety' under check_lectures§4. No exercise-style declarative-mislabeled-as-topic harm present.
